# Figures: Flows and systems

<!-- Generated by `npm run figures:docs` from src/components/figures/catalog.ts. Edit the catalogue, then run it again. -->

How does it work, and in what order? Diagrams of things that move: a user flow, a loop that feeds itself, a request between services, a journey with its low point, what happened when.

How to add one to an entry, and the rules they all follow: [figures.md](../figures.md).

In this file: [Flow](#flow) · [Loop](#loop) · [Sequence](#sequence) · [Journey](#journey) · [Timeline](#timeline)

## Flow

`D-01` · Boxes on a grid with routed arrows and dots that travel along them. It lays itself out for article and phone width.

**Use it for**

- Experiment and improvement, "What I built": the new path through the product, or how the parts fit.
- Review, "First run", when the path branches. AI work: an agent, its tools and what it reads.

**Not for:** A strict order between a few actors (Sequence), or a cycle (Loop). More than four columns: split the flow in two.

**Skills Map:** territories experience, engineering, ai; skills `user-flows`, `information-architecture`, `system-boundaries`, `system-dependencies`, `analytics-architecture`, `ai-agents`, `tool-calling`, `workflow-automation`, `ci-cd`

**Motion:** reveal, ambient

**Props**

- **`nodes`** *(required)* `{ id: string; label: string; detail?: string; col: number; row: number; kind?: 'step' | 'decision' | 'external' | 'store'; tone?: 'signal' | 'lit'; href?: string }[]`: `col` is the stage (from 0, the flow runs along it), `row` the lane. Up to four columns and three rows. `decision` is filled, `external` dashed (outside your system), `store` is where data rests. Keep `label` under 14 characters.
- **`edges`** *(required)* `{ from: string; to: string; label?: string; tone?: 'signal'; dashed?: boolean }[]`: Arrows by node id. An edge to an earlier column is drawn as a loop back. Two edges between the same nodes in one column, one each way, run side by side. `dashed` for something that happens later or only sometimes.
- **`stages`** `string[]`: A label for each column.
- **`motion`** `boolean`: Set to `false` for a still diagram. Default: dots travel along the arrows, with a pause button.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example: A user flow**

```mdx
<Flow
  title="Lesson first: the account comes after the value"
  stages={['Arrive', 'Try', 'Decide', 'Stay']}
  nodes={[
    { id: 'landing', label: 'Landing page', detail: 'Start a lesson', col: 0, row: 0 },
    {
      id: 'lesson',
      label: 'First lesson',
      detail: 'No account needed',
      col: 1,
      row: 0,
      tone: 'lit',
    },
    {
      id: 'prompt',
      label: 'Keep it?',
      detail: 'Asked after the lesson',
      col: 2,
      row: 0,
      kind: 'decision',
    },
    { id: 'account', label: 'Account', detail: 'Progress saved', col: 3, row: 0 },
    { id: 'guest', label: 'Guest', detail: 'Progress in this browser', col: 3, row: 1 },
  ]}
  edges={[
    { from: 'landing', to: 'lesson' },
    { from: 'lesson', to: 'prompt' },
    { from: 'prompt', to: 'account', label: 'Yes' },
    { from: 'prompt', to: 'guest', label: 'Not now' },
    { from: 'guest', to: 'lesson', label: 'Next visit', dashed: true },
  ]}
/>
```

**Example: How a system fits together**

```mdx
<Flow
  title="How an agent reads the Skills Map"
  nodes={[
    { id: 'agent', label: 'Agent', detail: 'Any MCP client', col: 0, row: 0, kind: 'external' },
    { id: 'mcp', label: 'MCP server', detail: 'Read-only tools', col: 1, row: 0 },
    { id: 'oauth', label: 'OAuth', detail: 'Sign in and approve', col: 1, row: 1 },
    {
      id: 'atlas',
      label: 'Skills Map',
      detail: 'Skills, resources, tools',
      col: 2,
      row: 0,
      kind: 'store',
    },
    {
      id: 'progress',
      label: 'Progress',
      detail: 'One status per skill',
      col: 2,
      row: 1,
      kind: 'store',
    },
  ]}
  edges={[
    { from: 'agent', to: 'mcp', label: 'Tool call', tone: 'signal' },
    { from: 'agent', to: 'oauth', label: 'First time', dashed: true },
    { from: 'mcp', to: 'atlas' },
    { from: 'mcp', to: 'progress', label: 'Signed in' },
  ]}
  evidence="observed"
  source="server/src/mcp.ts and server/README.md"
/>
```

## Loop

`D-02` · Three to six stages in a circle, with a dot going round and the stages listed beside it.

**Use it for**

- Retention work: the core loop, and which stage is weak.
- Distribution: a referral or content loop. Any process that feeds itself: build, measure, learn.

**Not for:** Steps that happen once. If the last stage does not lead back to the first, it is a Flow.

**Skills Map:** territories retention, distribution, cross-cutting; skills `core-loops`, `feedback-loops`, `referral-loops`, `habit-formation`, `network-effects`, `value-reinforcement`, `early-feedback`

**Motion:** reveal, ambient

**Props**

- **`stages`** *(required)* `{ label: string; note?: string; tone?: 'signal' | 'lit' }[]`: Three to six, clockwise from the top. `signal` marks the stage that is weak or under test, `lit` where the value is.
- **`center`** `string`: What goes round, written in the middle.
- **`sub`** `string`: A second line in the middle: how long one turn takes.
- **`motion`** `boolean`: Set to `false` for a still diagram.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Loop
  title="The loop the Skills Map is betting on"
  center="Weekly review"
  sub="One turn a week"
  stages={[
    { label: 'Look at your map', note: 'What did I work on this week?', tone: 'signal' },
    { label: 'Update statuses', note: 'Learning becomes comfortable.' },
    { label: 'Choose a focus', note: 'One territory you rarely touch.' },
    { label: 'Learn and apply', note: 'A resource, then a real problem.', tone: 'lit' },
  ]}
  caption="The first stage is the open question: nothing yet brings people back to the map."
  evidence="assumed"
  source="docs/product/PRODUCT.md, ledger 4"
/>
```

## Sequence

`D-03` · Who talks to whom, in order: actors as columns, messages as arrows that draw one after another.

**Use it for**

- Experiment and improvement, "What I built": a request across services, a sign-in round trip, a webhook.
- AI work: a model calling a tool and getting the result. Operations: a support hand-off.

**Not for:** More than four actors or ten messages. Branches: a sequence shows one path.

**Skills Map:** territories engineering, ai, operations; skills `api-design`, `authentication`, `async-systems`, `mcp`, `tool-calling`, `llm-integration`, `issue-investigation`, `support-workflows`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`actors`** *(required)* `{ id: string; label: string; kind?: 'system' | 'external' }[]`: Two to four, left to right. `external` is drawn dashed.
- **`messages`** *(required)* `{ from: string; to: string; label: string; kind?: 'call' | 'reply'; tone?: 'signal'; note?: string }[]`: In order, by actor id. `reply` is dashed. Keep `label` under 30 characters; a longer remark goes in `note` and is listed under the diagram.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Sequence
  title="An agent connects to the Skills Map for the first time"
  actors={[
    { id: 'agent', label: 'Agent', kind: 'external' },
    { id: 'mcp', label: '/mcp' },
    { id: 'auth', label: 'OAuth server' },
    { id: 'person', label: 'Person', kind: 'external' },
  ]}
  messages={[
    { from: 'agent', to: 'mcp', label: 'Call a tool' },
    { from: 'mcp', to: 'agent', label: '401, where to sign in', kind: 'reply' },
    { from: 'agent', to: 'auth', label: 'Authorize, with PKCE' },
    {
      from: 'auth',
      to: 'person',
      label: 'Approve this agent?',
      tone: 'signal',
      note: 'The only step a person sees. The rest happens between machines.',
    },
    { from: 'person', to: 'auth', label: 'Approve' },
    { from: 'auth', to: 'agent', label: 'Code, then tokens', kind: 'reply' },
    { from: 'agent', to: 'mcp', label: 'Call with the token' },
    { from: 'mcp', to: 'agent', label: 'Skills Map and statuses', kind: 'reply' },
  ]}
  evidence="observed"
  source={'server/README.md, "How an agent connects"'}
/>
```

## Journey

`D-04` · Steps along a line that rises and falls with how each one goes. The low point and the high point are marked.

**Use it for**

- Review, "First run" and "Where it loses people": the shape of the experience at a glance.
- Interview and observation: a user’s account of a week with the product.

**Not for:** Pretending to precision. The heights are a judgment: say whose in the caption and mark the evidence.

**Skills Map:** territories experience, discovery, activation; skills `journey-mapping`, `mental-models`, `cognitive-load`, `pain-points`, `expectation-setting`, `motivation`, `adoption-barriers`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`steps`** *(required)* `{ label: string; feel: number; note?: string; phase?: string }[]`: `feel` runs from -2 (stuck) to 2 (it clicks); 0 is neutral. Consecutive steps with the same `phase` are grouped under it.
- **`ends`** `{ low?: string; high?: string }`: Words at the ends of the scale. Default "Harder" and "Easier".
- **`mark`** `boolean`: Set to `false` to leave the low and high points unmarked.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Journey
  title="A new learner’s first week, as I read it"
  steps={[
    { label: 'Finds the app', feel: 0.5, phase: 'Arrive' },
    {
      label: 'Sign-up form',
      feel: -1.6,
      phase: 'Arrive',
      note: 'Six fields before anything happens.',
    },
    { label: 'Level test', feel: -0.6, phase: 'Set up' },
    {
      label: 'First lesson',
      feel: 1.7,
      phase: 'Learn',
      note: 'The first thing the app gives back.',
    },
    { label: 'Day 2 reminder', feel: 0.6, phase: 'Return' },
    { label: 'Streak lost', feel: -1, phase: 'Return', note: 'A missed day reads as failure.' },
  ]}
  evidence="illustrative"
  source="Example journey"
/>
```

## Timeline

`D-05` · Dated events down a rail, with decisions, releases, problems and results told apart.

**Use it for**

- Case study, "Context" and "Decisions": the history of the product.
- Experiment, "How I measured": the days it ran. Interview, "The decision": how it unfolded. An incident, from alert to fix.
- Profile: the versions of a product, each with a screenshot (`src`) of how it looked then.

**Not for:** Events with no dates or order. Durations: a timeline marks moments, not lengths.

**Skills Map:** territories shipping, operations, strategy, cross-cutting; skills `incident-response`, `roadmaps`, `lifecycle-stages`, `launch-planning`, `sequencing`, `reflection`, `product-narratives`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`events`** *(required)* `{ when: string; title: string; note?: string; kind?: 'event' | 'decision' | 'ship' | 'problem' | 'result'; src?: string; alt?: string }[]`: In order. `when` is a date, a time or a relative mark ("Day 3"). `kind` adds a tag and colours the marker. `src` adds a small screenshot of that moment beside the text (a phone screen, 240 px wide, under `/img/fieldwork/<entry>/`), for a history of versions; `alt` says what it shows.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Timeline
  title="The four weeks of the lesson-first experiment"
  events={[
    {
      when: '3 Nov',
      title: 'Hypothesis written',
      kind: 'decision',
      note: 'Metric, guardrails and the result that means keep, before any data.',
    },
    { when: '5 Nov', title: 'Out to the beta list', kind: 'ship' },
    { when: '9 Nov', title: 'Half of new visitors', kind: 'ship' },
    {
      when: '16 Nov',
      title: 'Accounts per visitor dip',
      kind: 'problem',
      note: 'Two days below the baseline, then back inside its usual range.',
    },
    { when: '1 Dec', title: 'Test ends', note: '2,000 visitors, split by visitor.' },
    {
      when: '2 Dec',
      title: 'Kept',
      kind: 'result',
      note: 'The interval for the difference is above zero.',
    },
  ]}
  evidence="illustrative"
  source="Example dates"
/>
```
